title: "Paired means and alignment"

For ordinary paired-mean inference, one first forms within-pair differences and then performs one-sample inference on those values. The UCCA question is different: it concerns absolute agreement of graph-derived Scene counts, so the focal statistic is a mean absolute difference.

## The general paired-mean result

For signed differences $D_i=Y_{i,A}-Y_{i,B}$, the target and estimator are

$$
\mu_D=\mathbb{E}[D]
\qquad\text{and}\qquad
\overline D=\frac{1}{n}\sum_{i=1}^nD_i.
$$

Under independent pairs with an appropriate t reference,

$$
\frac{\overline D-\mu_D}{S_D/\sqrt n}\sim t_{n-1},
$$

which yields

$$
\overline D\pm t_{1-\alpha/2,n-1}\frac{S_D}{\sqrt n}.
$$

This derivation remains useful, but it is not the analysis we impose on the UCCA alignment. The source passages are consecutive literary material rather than randomly sampled translation units, and the paper's agreement question is not a zero signed-mean test.

## The aligned agreement statistic

For source-order pair $i$, let $S_{i,\mathrm{en}}$ and $S_{i,\mathrm{fr}}$ denote Scene counts. Define

$$
\Delta_{\mathrm{aligned}}
=\frac{1}{n}\sum_{i=1}^n
\left|S_{i,\mathrm{fr}}-S_{i,\mathrm{en}}\right|.
$$

```{r}
#| label: ucca-aligned-difference
library(ggplot2)

ucca <- read.csv(
  "data/ucca-french-english/passage-counts.csv",
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)
english <- ucca[ucca$language == "en", ]
french <- ucca[ucca$language == "fr", ]
english <- english[order(english$pair_id), ]
french <- french[order(french$pair_id), ]
stopifnot(identical(english$pair_id, french$pair_id))

pairs <- data.frame(
  pair_id = english$pair_id,
  english_scenes = english$scene_count,
  french_scenes = french$scene_count,
  english_terminals = english$terminal_count,
  french_terminals = french$terminal_count
)
pairs$absolute_difference <- abs(pairs$french_scenes - pairs$english_scenes)
pairs$english_rate <- 100 * pairs$english_scenes / pairs$english_terminals
pairs$french_rate <- 100 * pairs$french_scenes / pairs$french_terminals

delta_aligned <- mean(pairs$absolute_difference)
rate_delta_aligned <- mean(abs(pairs$french_rate - pairs$english_rate))
stopifnot(abs(delta_aligned - 320 / 154) < 1e-12)

data.frame(
  pairs = nrow(pairs),
  mean_absolute_scene_difference = delta_aligned,
  mean_absolute_difference_per_100_terminals = rate_delta_aligned
)
```

The aligned passages differ by `r sprintf("%.3f", delta_aligned)` Scenes on average.

## A descriptive re-pairing reference

To show what the alignment contributes, we hold the English counts fixed and randomly permute the French passage order. Each draw measures how far arbitrary cross-language pairings lie apart.

```{r}
#| label: ucca-repairing
set.seed(20261018)
re_pairings <- 9999L
repaired_delta <- replicate(
  re_pairings,
  mean(abs(sample(pairs$french_scenes) - pairs$english_scenes))
)
lower_tail_fraction <-
  (1 + sum(repaired_delta <= delta_aligned)) / (re_pairings + 1)

stopifnot(abs(lower_tail_fraction - 0.0001) < 1e-12)

data.frame(
  aligned_difference = delta_aligned,
  mean_repaired_difference = mean(repaired_delta),
  minimum_repaired_difference = min(repaired_delta),
  maximum_repaired_difference = max(repaired_delta),
  descriptive_lower_tail_fraction = lower_tail_fraction
)
```

```{r}
#| label: plot-ucca-repairing
#| fig-cap: "Mean absolute Scene-count differences after arbitrary re-pairing. The line is the source-order aligned value."
ggplot(data.frame(mean_absolute_difference = repaired_delta),
       aes(mean_absolute_difference)) +
  geom_histogram(bins = 35, fill = "grey75", color = "white") +
  geom_vline(xintercept = delta_aligned, color = "#8B1A1A", linewidth = 0.7) +
  labs(x = "Mean absolute Scene-count difference after re-pairing",
       y = "Re-pairings") +
  theme_classic(base_size = 12)
```

The re-paired mean is `r sprintf("%.3f", mean(repaired_delta))` Scenes, and the plus-one lower-tail fraction is `r format(lower_tail_fraction, scientific = FALSE)`. This fraction is descriptive. It is not a randomization-test p value because translation alignment was not randomly assigned. The analysis supports an agreement claim for the pinned v2 passage graphs, not a general claim about languages, genres, or translators.

## Check your understanding

1. Why does the focal statistic use absolute rather than signed differences?
2. What feature changes across re-pairings?
3. Why is the lower-tail fraction not a randomization-test p value?
4. What does the per-terminal sensitivity calculation control?

<details class="understanding-answers">
<summary>Answers</summary>

1. Absolute differences measure passage-level count disagreement without allowing positive and negative signed differences to cancel. <!-- dqr-allow: empirical-answer -->
2. The French Scene counts are assigned to different English passages while each language's marginal counts remain fixed. <!-- dqr-allow: empirical-answer -->
3. Translation alignment was not randomly assigned, so permutation does not represent a randomized treatment assignment under a sharp null. <!-- dqr-allow: empirical-answer -->
4. Dividing by passage terminal counts controls descriptively for cross-passage and cross-language differences in passage length. <!-- dqr-allow: empirical-answer -->

</details>

The [independent-means page](independent-means.qmd) returns to Hillenbrand durations and combines uncertainty from two disjoint speaker groups.
